tutorial.title: Tutorial
tutorial.hint: Learn it in three minutes: from zero to one-click switching
tutorial.introBody: Think of connecting to an AI site like shipping a package: the URL is the address, the key is the signature proving you may ship, and the model is which route you pick. Changing sites used to mean filling in all three by hand - one typo and nothing sends. This extension bundles the three into a "site" and switches them all with one click on "Use" - connection only. It never touches your characters, presets, or prompts.
tutorial.step1Body: Click "Add site" and fill in three things: a name (anything, e.g. "Main daytime"), the API URL (like https://xxx/v1), and the API Key (masked by default; click "Show" to check it). Then click "Save site". Keys go into SillyTavern's built-in secret vault; the extension only remembers which one it used.
tutorial.step2Body: Click "Models" on the site card to open the picker: type in the search box to filter, check what you want, click "Add selected". The picker stays open, so keep searching and adding. You can also type model IDs manually when editing a site - separate multiple ones with commas.
tutorial.step3Body: Click "Use" - the extension runs four official SillyTavern commands to swap the connection, and "Switched to ..." means it worked. Click a model row to switch models. The ⚡ ball (floating quick-switch) switches anytime; both the ball and the window can be dragged.
tutorial.floatBody: Check "Enable floating quick-switch window" in settings to get the ⚡ ball: click the ball to open/close the panel, click a site name to switch, click the model button to expand the model list. Sites show 4 per page — use the Previous / Next buttons at the bottom when you have more. Positions are remembered.
tutorial.keyBody: The key field accepts several keys separated by commas; the first is the default. The key button on the card rotates between them - handy when one key runs out of quota.
tutorial.groupBody: When sites pile up, group them and filter with the group buttons on top; the up/down buttons on each card set your own order, which survives reloads and restarts.
tutorial.statsBody: After each switch and a successful generation, the current site gains one "Used nx". Stats stay on this device, never affect sorting, and can be cleared with "Reset usage stats".
tutorial.ioBody: "Export" saves the site list to a JSON file, keys excluded by default; on a new machine or after a reinstall, "Import" merges it back by name + URL. Checking "Include keys when exporting" asks for confirmation and adds an INCLUDES-KEYS- prefix to the filename - treat that file like a password.
tutorial.langBody: Choose "Follow SillyTavern / Chinese / English" in settings; it applies instantly.
tutorial.outroTitle: That is it - you are ready
tutorial.outroBody: Now click "Add site" and walk your own first site through the three steps. If "Fetch models" fails (some sites block direct browser requests), just type model IDs manually - everything else still works.
wand.title: Quick API Switch
wand.hint: Tap a model row to switch · tap a site row to expand
tutorial.wandBody: The wand (✨) menu next to the chat input has an "API Quick Switch" entry. It opens a large panel: use the search box to filter sites or models, tap a site row to expand its model list, tap a model row to switch. The panel stays open after a switch so you can switch several in a row; sites show 4 per page — use the Previous / Next buttons at the bottom of the panel when you have more, and close it with the × in the top-right corner. On phones the panel appears right above the wand button, so you never have to reach for the ⚡ ball.
